title: What is the Oliver Wyman interview process, and how should you prepare?
description: Oliver Wyman's hiring steps: online test, screening interview, case and fit rounds, and the written case used in some offices.
hook: Oliver Wyman is a major strategy firm with particular strength in financial services, and its process is known for being thorough. The part that catches people out is the written case, so give it real attention.
body:
The steps

Prep guides describe five stages: an online application, an online test, a screening interview, a first round of case and fit interviews, and a final round that adds more cases and, in some offices, a written case. The final round is often a "super day" of back-to-back interviews with principals and partners.

The cases

Oliver Wyman cases are usually candidate-led, like BCG and Bain. Expect solid maths.

The written case

You receive a pack with a business scenario and data, prepare alone for a set time, then present your recommendation. Many candidates run out of time by reading everything in detail. Skim first, find the question, pick the few exhibits that matter and build a short, clear answer. More on written cases.

How to prepare

  • Practise candidate-led cases with strong maths.
  • Practise at least two written cases against the clock.
  • Prepare fit stories and a specific answer to why Oliver Wyman.

Sources

  • Hacking the Case Interview: Oliver Wyman interview process
  • Hacking the Case Interview: Oliver Wyman final round
  • IGotAnOffer: Oliver Wyman case interview

Checked November 2026. Processes change by office and year, so always confirm with the firm's own careers page and your recruiter.

Practise decisions under commercial constraints

An original practice scenario: an insurer considers launching a telematics policy for younger drivers. Begin with the objective, likely customer demand and pricing competitiveness. Then calculate expected claims, acquisition expense and the cost of installing or processing the technology. Ask whether the client can differentiate risks well enough to attract good customers without unintentionally selecting the riskiest drivers.

Suppose annual premium is £1,000 per customer, expected claims are £650, servicing costs £100 and acquisition costs £120. First-year contribution is £130 per policy before central overhead and capital costs. If the acquisition spend is genuinely one-off, the contribution in renewal years could be higher, but only if claims and retention behave as expected.

Explain the uncertainties that would change your answer: claims frequency, fraud, regulation, data consent and renewals. Ask your recruiter whether the interview includes a written case, quantitative exercise or standard live case, and practise that format. Published candidate experiences are useful context, but cannot establish a universal Oliver Wyman interview sequence.
